messages:
maya: ran PTQ-int8 canary for heron-v2 on the funcall benchmark set. hit ~0.84% total funcall schema failures. a bunch look like duplicate keys + type flips in streaming output. sample below — reproduced on canary_gpu_3

maya: ```
STREAM_PART: {"tool":"get_user","args":{"id":"123","id":123}}
STREAM_PART: {"tool":"get_user","args":{"id":123,
"name":"alice",�}}
```

maya: also saw a few outputs with a trailing NUL (�) right before the closing brace which breaks our ndjson/stream-merge.

ci-bot: canary summary: runs=5000, failures=42, duplicate-key=30, type-mismatch=8, trailing-null=4 — rolling to baseline if failures > 1% :rotating_light:

chet: ugh. can you paste the minimal reproducer (command + model args) so I can run locally? :eyes:

maya: sure — quick repro we used: `./tools/run_canary --model heron-v2-ptq --tasks funcall --streaming true --seed 42 --runs 1000`

maya: logs + one raw stream capture: `s3://canary/1765436789/raw_stream.tar.gz`

chet: thanks. short guess: either quant-induced tokenizer splitting causing interleaved tokens or streaming buffer boundary interleaving two partial JSON writes. can you try `--streaming false` to see if non-stream path has same issue?

maya: did that — streaming=false drops failures to 0.2% and duplicate-key count goes down a lot. so it's streaming-specific.

sylvia: interesting. this smells like the streaming writer flattens token chunks without consistent kv-order, and PTQ changed tokenization distribution so numeric tokens split differently. i can repro quickly by forcing `--tokenizer legacy` vs `--tokenizer bpe` — will check.

kevin: fwiw we shipped a kernel tweak last week that changed float->int token rounding for speed (commit 7f3d2a). it made some numeric tokens merge differently in int encodings. try `QUANT_ROUND_MODE=nearest` to emulate old behaviour.

maya: quick smoke with `QUANT_ROUND_MODE=nearest ./tools/run_canary --model heron-v2-ptq --tasks funcall --streaming true --runs 1000` — failures dropped from 42 -> 9. duplicate-key -> 6. trailing-null unchanged (still 4).

chet: good signal. so two orthogonal problems: 1) quant rounding/tokenization diffs -> duplicate keys, 2) streaming flush adds spurious nulls at chunk boundary.

chet: short-term mitigation: add a streaming postprocessor that merges sequential JSON fragments and dedup keys (prefer last), plus strip control chars before parse. small change, low risk.

maya: can we do that in canary harness so we don't get noisy alerts while we root cause?

ci-bot: opened ticket ML-1229: "streaming-parse-dedupe-and-control-char-strip for canary" and attached canary log.

sylvia: i'll draft a tiny PR to the streaming parser to ignore control chars (�, ) and collapse duplicate keys. will add a feature flag `STREAM_PARSE_DEDUPE=true` so we can gate it.

kevin: parallel-track: i'll try to reproduce with a non-PTQ build on same seed to isolate kernel vs quant. if it's quant only we may revert the rounding change or add a quant-aware tokenizer patch.

maya: thanks. i'll keep the canary pinned to `QUANT_ROUND_MODE=nearest` for now and mute alerts for this run. will follow up with short writeup once sylvia's PR is up. :thumbsup:

sylvia: PR draft done — assigning to chet for review. will run canary with flag set after merge and report numbers.

chet: ack, will review today. if green we can enable in canary harness and then plan a proper root cause dive next sprint.

maya: tagging infra: @kevin for kernel repro and @sylvia for parser PR. moving to action items.
